title: The suite builds the exact input that deadlocks the review queue, then asserts something else
detail: Line 149 seeds a card with `options: []` — precisely the state that permanently jams ReviewPage (S106) — and the test only checks that the card is deleted along with its book. The fixture for the worst bug in the feature already exists in the test file; nobody ever asserted what the UI does with it. One `render(<ReviewPage/>)` and one assertion away.

title: The seam carrying the most defects has no integration test at all
detail: Nothing anywhere mocks @google/genai and asserts what the app does with a malformed response, a 429, a safety block, or an empty response.text. errors.test.ts unit-tests toAiError in isolation, which is the mapping — not the seam. Every 'unvalidated model JSON reaches IndexedDB' finding (S032, S062, S141-S144, F005, F030, F034, F035) lives on a boundary that no test crosses, so all of them can regress silently.

title: The 'no Gemini call on boot' test passes vacuously if fetch is never called
detail: `for (const call of fetchSpy.mock.calls) expect(...)` runs zero assertions on an empty array, so the test is green whether the stub worked, whether the SDK bypassed global fetch, or whether the app genuinely made no call. It cannot distinguish 'correct' from 'not actually testing anything'. It needs a positive control — assert the spy was installed and that a deliberate AI action does hit it.

title: A tautological test asserts the test environment, not the app
detail: `it('exposes indexedDB to tests')` checks that globalThis.indexedDB is defined — a property of vitest's setup file, not of BookSum. It can only fail if the harness is misconfigured, in which case every other test in the file fails first. It inflates the count by one and proves nothing.

title: The migration test file has eleven tests and none touches the field the known migration bug is in
detail: It asserts summaryId is set (line 107) but never asserts Book.oneSentenceTakeaway, which migration does not populate — so every migrated book renders 'Not summarised yet' despite having a summary. Also untested: a legacy book with no summary data at all (which still gets a summaryId and an empty Summary, S013), and more than one legacy user, even though legacyUserIds() loops.

title: The hook-probe pattern leaks state through a module-level binding
detail: `let api` at module scope is reassigned on every render of every test in the file, and assertions read it after awaits. It works only because vitest runs tests in a file serially, and it makes each test's assertions depend on which render happened last rather than on an explicit handle. The same pattern is repeated in useLibrary.test.tsx.

title: Cascade tests cover the happy path only, and reviewCards has no direct tests
detail: Both cascade tests assert successful deletion; neither exercises a mid-cascade failure, which is exactly the non-atomic gap in S006/S007. The reviewCards module — listDue, listByProfile, listByBook, removeByBook — has no test file of its own and is covered only incidentally through the review-queue hook. No test asserts that deleting a profile removes its review cards.

title: The UUID assertion is unanchored
detail: `toMatch(/[0-9a-f-]{36}/)` passes for any string that merely contains 36 such characters, so it would accept a malformed id with a prefix. Anchoring it costs two characters.

title: Setup and fixtures are re-declared across roughly eight test files
detail: `beforeEach(resetDb + localStorage.clear)` appears in most suites, and seedProfile / bookInput / renderQueue / mount are re-implemented per file with small variations. A shared test-utils module would remove around a hundred lines and make the variations deliberate rather than accidental.

title: Logging is unstructured, unprefixed, and duplicated against the toast it accompanies
detail: Nine console calls across seven files, each a bare string plus a raw error, with no shared prefix to filter on and no distinction between a handled failure and a real fault. Five of them log the error AND surface a toast for the same event, so the console double-reports. There is no way for a user reporting a bug to tell which console lines belong to BookSum.

title: Compliance summary: theme fails, mobile fails, security claim fails, cost passes
detail: Reading the contract as it applies to a standalone app — THEME: fails, ~40 sites render wrong in one mode including four primary buttons that vanish (S039-S041, S046-S050, S058, S086, S100, S174). MOBILE: fails, no navigation below 640px (S091). SECURITY: fails, an inoperative encryption toggle is displayed as active (S081). COST: passes — BYOK means the maintainer pays nothing, though quiz generation re-fires on object identity (S057). ACCESSIBILITY, if counted: fails, the library grid and stats filters are mouse-only (S161, S112).
